item.title: Anthropic says scientists used AI for possible biological weapons development
item.description: Anthropic said it blocked scientists who used its Claude AI models "in ways that could support biological weapons development."

item.title: Why you shouldn't bank on Trump's $5,000 dividends happening
item.description: President Trump pledged $5,000 to all American adults if Republicans retain control of Congress. You may not be able to take that to the bank.

item.title: Squeeze your knees and 2 other things to know when donating blood
item.description: Dr. Courtney Lawrence from the Red Cross shared with Norah O'Donnell on "Healthful" the three things people should know when they donate blood.

item.title: White House framework for testing new AI models remains hidden as concerns mount
item.description: The White House has not publicly released the voluntary framework for testing frontier AI models that it finalized in August.

item.title: Iran strikes U.S. jets after Trump promises war to end after midterms
item.description: U.S. jets were hit by Iranian missiles while parked at a base in Jordan, sources tell CBS News, while Trump said the war will end "immediately" after midterms.

item.title: George W. Bush says Americans "don't pay attention to the lesson of 9/11"
item.description: Former President George W. Bush gave rare remarks on Wednesday as Americans mark 25 years since the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.

item.title: Kevin Reddington files motion to toss mistrial, acquit Lindsay Clancy
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense attorney, Kevin Reddington, filed a motion Thursday to throw out last week's mistrial and acquit Clancy. Clancy admitted to killing her three children, but pled not guilty to murder charges, arguing she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

item.title: How political violence shifted after Charlie Kirk was fatally shot
item.description: Instances of political violence continued after Charlie Kirk was fatally shot during a Utah college event. CBS News' Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Trump administration officials remember Charlie Kirk a year after his killing
item.description: It has been one year since conservative political activist Charlie Kirk was fatally shot during an event in Utah. Benji Backer, the founder and CEO of Nature Is Nonpartisan, joins CBS News with more on his friendship with Kirk.

item.title: Ross Fire still burning, with over 90,000 acres scorched
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: Lawsuit seeks to block deployment of ICE, federal agents to polling sites
item.description: A coalition of advocacy groups and a Democratic-led city filed a preemptive lawsuit seeking to block the Trump administration from deploying armed ICE agents to polling sites ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Lawsuit seeks order to prevent ICE agents from being deployed to voting sites for the midterms
item.description: A lawsuit seeks to preemptively block the Trump administration from sending ICE agents to polling sites during the November elections. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez reports.

item.title: Anthropic reveals another AI hacking incident, the fourth of its kind
item.description: Anthropic disclosed another AI hacking incident involving one of its earlier models. Forum AI's Robbie Goldfarb joins CBS News with more context.

item.title: Evidence could change our understanding of 9/11 attacks 25 years ago | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: Videos and documents turned over to the FBI in the weeks after 9/11, including video of the Capitol and an airplane sketch, have raised new questions for investigators.

item.title: Trump pitches $5,000 payments, but only if GOP wins House and Senate
item.description: President Trump vowed Wednesday to send a $5,000 "dividend" to every American citizen after the midterms, but only if Republicans hold onto control of Congress. He didn't offer details on how the payments would work.

item.title: Appeals court declines to lift block on Postal Service rule for mail ballots
item.description: A federal appeals court denied the Trump administration's request to lift a lower court's order that blocked new rules for mail ballots before the midterms.

item.title: Rolling over a 401(k) to gold? What to check before you move your money
item.description: A gold rollover can reshape your retirement portfolio, making it important to know what you're signing up for.

item.title: A 9/11 memorial is unfinished and in disrepair. A first responder is pushing for its restoration.
item.description: Advocates for New Jersey's "Empty Sky" 9/11 memorial say the monument has fallen into disrepair and needs to be completed. First responder Kathe Conlon explains why the memorial matters and remembers her team's rescue efforts after the September 11, 2001, attacks.

item.title: Is $10,000 in credit card debt enough for debt forgiveness?
item.description: A five-figure credit card balance can be tough to tackle, but does it make debt forgiveness a realistic option?

item.title: Daughters of 9/11 victims seek answers about accused mastermind's trial
item.description: A new documentary, "Daughters of 9/11," follows their pursuit of information and closure, which they were determined to find for themselves, other families who lost loved ones in the attacks and the American public.

item.title: First-ever adult T. rex trackway found in North Dakota
item.description: Paleontologists have identified the first known trackway made by a full-grown Tyrannosaurus rex, and the discovery was made in the North Dakota badlands.

item.title: Trump touts "great conversation" with Putin on ending the war in Ukraine
item.description: Russian attacks continue to ravage Ukraine. President Trump says he spoke with President Vladimir Putin about ending the war. Plus, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's plane was nearly struck by a Russian drone, according to Norway's prime minister. CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Supreme Court blocks Missouri from using new map favoring GOP in fall elections
item.description: The Supreme Court said Missouri must use a 2022 congressional map — not a new congressional map that favors Republicans — in the 2026 midterm elections.

item.title: The OpenAI-Hugging Face hack was just the beginning, experts say
item.description: "What happens inside frontier AI companies now clearly affects everyone outside of them," an expert said following the hack on Hugging Face by AI agents being tested by OpenAI.

item.title: Stella Parton says her sister Dolly was prepared and at peace when she died
item.description: Stella Parton gives insight into her sister Dolly Parton's marriage, makeup habits and views on death in an exclusive CBS News interview.

item.title: Deadly fire on ferry off Philippines leaves dozens of people missing
item.description: A fire on a passenger ferry off the western Philippines left dozens of people missing and killed at least five. An intense and widespread search was on for the unaccounted for.

item.title: Inside the 29 minutes that captured 9/11: CBS News cameraman reflects on what he saw at Ground Zero
item.description: CBS News cameraman Mark LaGanga captured the 29 minutes in between the towers falling on 9/11, even filming as the North Tower collapsed around him. Twenty-five years later, he reflects on his experience in an interview with 60 Minutes digital.

item.title: Barry Melrose, prominent NHL player, coach and broadcaster, dies at 70
item.description: Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died at 70.

item.title: New documentary looks at generation that grew up after 9/11 attacks
item.description: A new Netflix documentary is out about those who were children in the wake of the 9/11 attacks. "Turning Point: Generation 9/11" profiles people whose parents died on that day, as well as soldiers who joined the military because of 9/11. Director Brian Knappenberger joins "The Takeout" to discuss the making of the film.

item.title: Rep. Lori Trahan says it's time for Congress to "finally get off the sidelines" and regulate AI
item.description: An employee for the artificial intelligence company Anthropic has resigned over concerns that AI could spiral out of control and destroy humanity. Democratic Rep. Lori Trahan of Massachusetts, a staunch advocate for AI regulation, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.
